speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. I see you have concerns about shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain radiates to your teeth or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timing of the shooting pain when eating is highly suggestive of a specific nerve issue; do you feel any tingling, numbness, or a "pins and needles" sensation in the lower lip, chin, or tongue? Also, have you noticed any changes in your sensation on the ear canal or the pinna itself?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia.

The combination of shooting ear pain triggered specifically by eating (jaw movement) and discomfort when wearing earrings (pinna manipulation) in the context of your recent tympanoplasty and history of ear infections is highly characteristic of this condition. Given your improved hearing and lack of reported motor deficits in the face, I do not suspect a major nerve injury like a facial nerve palsy. Does the pain feel like an electric shock, and does the area around your ear feel sensitive to the touch?
